variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
let x: int = 10;
const y: int = 20;
variables.notes: `let` is used for variable bindings and `const` for constants.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Hare has fixed size integers and standard primitive types.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
let z = x + y;
let b = x > y;
operators.notes: Standard operators, note the mandatory semicolons.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals require parentheses and a semicolon at the end of the block.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: `for` is also used for while loops.

functions.title: Functions

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
// Hare does not have built-in map types.
// You must implement or use a hash map struct from a library.
maps.notes: Hare is a minimalist systems language and lacks a built-in map type.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Hare uses tagged unions and pattern matching for errors.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Hare uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Hare provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Hare uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Hare supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Hare distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Hare supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.notes: Hare evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.notes: Hare represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: Hare implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Hare models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: Hare manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Hare represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: Hare provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: Hare structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
